 Massachusetts couple discovers surprising series of connections while wedding planning: "What are the odds of that?"
 By
 Juli McDonald 
 Juli McDonald 
 Juli McDonald is a general assignment reporter for WBZ-TV.
 Read Full Bio 
 Juli McDonald 
 Updated on: October 20, 2026 / 9:05 AM EDT 
 / CBS Boston
 Add CBS News on Google 
 Sometimes the best love stories come with a surprise that you never saw coming.
 A newlywed couple in Franklin, Massachusetts, recently discovered that their connection goes all the way back to their baptism.
 "It was junior year of college and he did tell me that we were going to get married the day that he met me," recalled Jessica McGinty, laughing.
 It was love at first sight for Ryan McGinty, when then-Jessica Connolly came to visit her friends at his college campus. Quite the meet-cute for these now newlyweds, who grew up in neighboring Westwood and Walpole. 
 "Seven minutes away from each other our whole life and didn't know each other," she said.
 Complete strangers, but both belonged to St. Timothy Catholic Church in Norwood. 
 "My dad's still a lector here," said Ryan McGinty. "We still come here. This is probably the best place to be because this is where we've been our whole lives."
 Ryan and Jessica McGinty 
 Amanda Curry Photography
 They grew up in different towns, had different friends, and went to different colleges. But when planning the details of their wedding day, God's divine direction in their lives was clear - he makes everything beautiful in its time. 
 "Our moms both knew it was a day in February, and it was freezing cold, it was our baptism," Jessica explained, of piecing it all together.
 "I was looking at the registry books and sure enough they were baptized together," said pastoral associate Michelle Gallo. 
 "I decided to look at the other sacraments, sure enough, first communion, confirmation, and now wedding. What are the odds of that? To think that you were together to receive all those graces four times? That's pretty special."
 And as they look ahead to their future, the couple feels so blessed to build on this strong foundation, with supportive families, a parish that feels like home, and a real respect and admiration for each other. 
 "Even when I'm having a bad day, come home from work and I'm maybe in a bad mood, I still feel Ryan's love all the time," Jessica said. 
 "You would have a really hard time with all the people that know her, to find one person that had a bad thing to say about her," her husband added.
